ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Introduce the background and motivation for hierarchical text classification (HTC).
content_points: Text classification is widely used in NLP applications like sentiment analysis and document categorization.
Hierarchical text classification (HTC) is a multi-label classification problem with a taxonomic hierarchy.
The taxonomic hierarchy is modeled as a tree or directed acyclic graph.

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Highlight the gaps and limitations in current HTC methods.
content_points: Local approaches construct multiple models but lack holistic structural information.
Global approaches treat HTC as flat MLC but ignore fine-grained label correlations.
No existing method encodes holistic label structure for label correlation features.

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Present the key insight and contributions of the proposed Hi-AGM model.
content_points: Formulate the hierarchy as a directed graph with prior probabilities of label dependencies.
Introduce Hi-AGM with hierarchy-aware structure encoders (TreeLSTM or hierarchy-GCN).
Two variants: HiAGM-LA (inductive) and HiAGM-TP (deductive) for feature aggregation.

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: To categorize and explain existing approaches in hierarchical text classification
content_points: Local approaches: LCN, LCPN, LCL
Global approaches: modifications of flat MLC models
Deep learning architectures in global models
Attention mechanism in MLC

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: To visualize the taxonomic hierarchy used in hierarchical text classification
content_points: Nodes represent categories
Edges indicate parent-child relationships
Prior probabilities reflect label dependencies
Guides label embedding and feature propagation

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: To highlight the differences and improvements of the proposed method
content_points: Previous models focus on improving decoders
HiAGM extracts label-wise text features with hierarchy encoders
HiAGM-LA employs multi-label attention with simplified structure encoder
Reduces computational complexity

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Introduce the concept and structure of hierarchical text classification
content_points: Hierarchical text classification (HTC) organizes labels with a predefined taxonomic hierarchy
Hierarchy groups label subsets based on class relations
Taxonomic hierarchy can be tree-like or DAG structure
DAG can be converted to tree-like structure by distinguishing single-path nodes

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Present the mathematical formulation of the HTC problem
content_points: Taxonomic hierarchy formulated as directed graph G = (V, E, E)
V = set of label nodes, E = top-down and bottom-up hierarchy paths
HTC defined as H = (X, L) with text objects X and label sets L
Each sample corresponds to multiple classes in hierarchy paths
Sample belongs to parent node if condition pertains to child node

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Introduce the overall architecture of the proposed HiAGM model
content_points: HiAGM leverages fine-grained hierarchy information for text classification
Consists of text encoder for textual information and hierarchy-aware structure encoder
Two variants: HiAGM-LA (multi-label attention) and HiAGM-TP (text feature propagation)

ppt_outline.slide_title: HiAGM Variants: LA and TP Approaches
ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Detail the two different approaches for hybrid information aggregation
content_points: HiAGM-LA: updates label representations with structure encoder
HiAGM-LA: generates label-aware text features via multi-label attention
HiAGM-TP: propagates text representations through hierarchy
HiAGM-TP: obtains label-wise features with fused label correlations

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Introduce the concept of taxonomic hierarchy and its importance in hierarchical text classification
content_points: Taxonomic hierarchy describes hierarchical relations among labels
Major bottleneck: how to effectively utilize this established structure
Previous methods use static hierarchy paths in pipeline frameworks
HiAGM leverages prior knowledge of label correlations

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Explain the Bayesian statistical approach for encoding hierarchical relationships
content_points: Edge feature f(e_i,j) represented by prior probabilities P(U_j|U_i) and P(U_i|U_j)
Conditional probability P(U_j|U_i) = N_j/N_i where N_k is occurrence count
Reverse conditional P(U_i|U_j) always 1.0 due to hierarchy constraint
Prior probabilities rescaled and normalized for child nodes

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Show the overall architecture of the hierarchy-aware global model
content_points: Integrates text encoding with hierarchical label structure modeling
Two variants: HiAGM-LA (Multi-Label Attention) and HiAGM-TP (Message Propagation)
HiAGM-LA uses soft attention for label-aware text feature fusion
HiAGM-TP directly propagates text features through hierarchy

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Introduce the concept and components of the hierarchy-aware structure encoder
content_points: Tree-LSTM and GCN as base structure encoders
Bidirectional Tree-LSTM for label correlation induction
Hierarchy-GCN for directed hierarchy graph processing
Fine-grained hierarchy information modeling

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Detail the bidirectional Tree-LSTM implementation
content_points: Childsum module for bottom-up aggregation
Top-down module for parent-to-child propagation
Concatenation of bidirectional hidden states
Mini-batch training enabled by fixed hierarchy

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Explain the Hierarchy-GCN's edge-weighted aggregation
content_points: Top-down, bottom-up and self-loop edges
Weighted adjacency matrix for hierarchy probabilities
Direction-specific transformations
ReLU activation for final node representations

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Present key equations governing hierarchy propagation
content_points: Input/output gate mechanisms
Memory cell updates with edge-wise flow factors
Hierarchical probability weight calculations
Bidirectional state fusion

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Introduce the end-to-end hierarchy-aware global model and its two variants
content_points: HiAGM combines traditional text classification with hierarchy encoder for label-wise text features
Two variants: HiAGM-LA (parallel model for inductive fusion) and HiAGM-TP (serial model for deductive fusion)
Model processes token embeddings through bidirectional GRU and CNNs for text representation
Top-k max-pooling extracts key information from n-gram features
Continuous text representation S obtained with dimension dc

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Detail the inductive fusion approach using multi-label attention
content_points: Simplifies multi-label attention LCL models to a global model
Enhances label representations with bidirectional hierarchical information
Overcomes convergence problem for label embedding across levels
Uses trainable label embedding Lk and structure encoders
Calculates label-wise attention value αki for inductive fusion

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Explain the deductive variant using hierarchical text feature propagation
content_points: Conducts propagation of text features through hierarchy encoder
Transforms text features S to node inputs V via linear transformation
Updates textual information through same holistic taxonomic hierarchy
Output hidden state h represents deductive hierarchy-aware text features
Higher computational complexity but easier convergence compared to HiAGM-LA

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Explain the process of flattening the hierarchy for classification and the final prediction layer
content_points: Flatten hierarchy by treating all nodes as leaf nodes for multi-label classification
Final hierarchy-aware features fed into a fully connected layer for prediction
Complementary with recursive regularization for parameter optimization

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Detail the loss functions used for training the HiAGM model
content_points: Recursive regularization loss ensures parameter consistency between parent and child nodes
Binary cross-entropy loss function for multi-label classification
Final loss combines classification loss and recursive regularization with weighting factor

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Introduce the datasets, evaluation metrics, and implementation details
content_points: Description of benchmark datasets used
Evaluation metrics for performance comparison
Implementation details of Hi-AGM variants

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Present the main experimental results and comparisons with existing methods
content_points: Performance comparison of HiAGM-LA and HiAGM-TP
Comparison with state-of-the-art methods
Significant improvements on benchmark datasets

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Discuss the ablation study and deeper analysis of experimental results
content_points: Impact of hierarchy-aware structure encoders
Effectiveness of label-aware text features
Analysis of text feature propagation

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Introduce the benchmark datasets used for evaluation
content_points: RCV1-V2 and NYT are news categorization corpora
WOS includes abstracts from Web of Science
All datasets annotated with hierarchical taxonomic labels
Different splitting strategies for each dataset
Special handling of samples with no label or single-level label

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Explain the performance measurement approach
content_points: Standard metrics: Micro-F1 and Macro-F1
Micro-F1 considers overall precision/recall
Macro-F1 averages F1-scores across labels
Micro-F1 weights frequent labels more
Macro-F1 treats all labels equally

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Describe model architecture and training configuration
content_points: Bi-GRU with 64 hidden units + 3 parallel CNN layers
300D GloVe embeddings with OOV handling
Maximum input length of 256 tokens
Adam optimizer with specific hyperparameters
Different dropout rates per layer

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Show quantitative performance improvements of HiAGM variants against baselines
content_points: HiAGM-LA achieves 61.90% Macro-F1 and 82.54% Micro-F1
HiAGM-TP obtains best performance: 63.35% Macro-F1 and 83.96% Micro-F1
Both variants outperform state-of-the-art HTC studies
Demonstrates advancement of hierarchy encoders

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Demonstrate core architecture effectiveness independent of regularization
content_points: HiAGM variants show competitive improvement without recursive regularization
1.75% (HiAGM-LA) and 3.13% (HiAGM-TP) Macro-F1 gains over HiLAP
Recursive regularization is complementary but not necessary
Proves intrinsic strength of hierarchy-aware architecture

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Show generalization capability across multiple benchmarks
content_points: HiAGM achieves consistent improvements on RCV1-V2, WOS and NYT
Strong performance on data-sparse classes deep in hierarchy
Particularly excels in Macro-F1 scores
Demonstrates global model's text feature enhancement capability

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Show the superior performance of HiAGM variants over baselines
content_points: Both HiAGM-LA and HiAGM-TP outperform baseline models and previous studies
HiAGM-TP shows better performance than HiAGM-LA with both encoders
HiAGM-LA is more computationally efficient during inference
HiAGM-TP recommended for high performance, HiAGM-LA for faster inference

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Analyze the effect of GCN depth on model performance
content_points: One-layer GCN consistently performs best in both variants
Deeper networks may introduce noise from non-adjacent node correlations
Local hierarchical relationships sufficient for effective aggregation
Findings align with recursive regularization principles

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Evaluate different prior probability configurations
content_points: Fixed weighted adjacent matrix outperforms unweighted and trainable ones
Best results obtained when following hierarchy direction
Trainable priors offer higher flexibility and better performance
Interactions between non-adjacent nodes negatively impact performance

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Demonstrate performance gains across hierarchical levels
content_points: Both HiAGM variants outperform baseline at all levels
Significant advantage observed at deeper levels (4-8)
HiAGM-TP shows stronger feature propagation in deep structures
Consistent superiority of hierarchy-aware models

ppt_outline.slide_purpose: Summarize the main contributions and achievements of the research
content_points: Proposed an end-to-end hierarchy-aware global model for hierarchical text classification
Introduced bidirectional TreeLSTM and hierarchy-GCN as structure encoders
Developed two variants: multi-label attention (HiAGM-LA) and text feature propagation (HiAGM-TP)
Achieved significant improvements on three benchmark datasets
Obtained state-of-the-art results on RCV1-V2 (Macro-F1: 63.35%, Micro-F1: 83.96%)
